title: I'm Not on the DEV Team. I Still Debugged Their Missing Badges From Public Code. (And My First Test Was Wrong.)
why_read: A readable, honest personal account of diagnosing a real bug in a large open-source Rails app purely from public code, with a genuine lesson about misleading test results.
analysis: The author, an outside contributor to the Forem (DEV.to) codebase, traces why multi-commit contributor badges weren't being awarded and ships a fix merged by the project's creator. The piece specifically highlights a false-positive test, a test that passed despite not actually verifying the intended behavior, which is a useful and common pitfall worth internalizing. This is a modest but genuine war story about debugging and test correctness in a real production codebase. It's a small-scale but honest technical narrative rather than a deep or broadly impactful finding.
